expectations.text: Response lists the required DESIGN subagent brief anatomy fields: Product/brand identity, Goal, Vibe, Target location, and Variant hypothesis.
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly lists and defines all five: 'Product / Brand Identity (1–2 vivid sentences)', 'Goal', 'Vibe (one natural-language feeling — NOT a design style name)', 'Target Location (file path, canvas shape ID, dev server URL)', 'Variant Hypothesis'.

expectations.text: Response explicitly states NOT to include specific CSS values, colours, font names, pixel spacing, layout prescriptions, section names, or design style names.
expectations.evidence: Response provides a full 'Must Omit' table listing: 'Specific CSS values (colours, hex codes, px spacing, opacity)', 'Font names or typography specs', 'Layout prescriptions', 'Section names or content order', 'Design style names ("minimalist", "material design", "flat", "neumorphic")'.

expectations.text: Response says each subagent must get a distinct brief — a different variant hypothesis — so they produce genuinely distinct output rather than three nearly identical variants.
expectations.evidence: Response states: 'Each subagent gets a different vibe. Giving both subagents the same vibe produces nearly identical variants — a documented mistake in the skill.' and shows distinct briefs for each subagent.

expectations.text: Response describes the variant labelling convention: label by design hypothesis not letter alone — e.g. 'A — Minimal' / 'B — Editorial' / 'C — Bold' — so the user can say 'I prefer B' precisely.
expectations.evidence: Response states: 'Never label variants by letter alone ("A", "B") — the design hypothesis name makes approval conversations precise. When the user says "I prefer B," they mean the editorial direction, not an anonymous slot.' Shows example labels 'A — Cockpit' and 'B — Editorial'.
